models.name: Model A: Steady Newtonian CFD
models.what_it_computes: Pressure–flow relationship (hydraulic resistance), distribution of outflow between end-hole and side-holes, and local wall shear along the terminal segment under laminar, incompressible, Newtonian assumptions with rigid walls.

models.name: Model B: Shear-thinning CFD with surface roughness
models.what_it_computes: Hydraulic resistance and flow partitioning using a Carreau–Yasuda rheology for dialysate, incorporating effective wall roughness and no-slip to capture biofilm-textured surfaces.

models.name: Model C: Porous-jump hole occlusion CFD
models.what_it_computes: Hydraulic resistance and hole-by-hole flow using porous-jump boundary conditions at lateral ports to represent partial occlusion coupled with a Newtonian bulk flow model.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 1: Lateral-hole–dominated drainage with partial occlusion
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Early fibrin or omental contact can elevate entrance losses at side-holes, shifting resistance upstream and limiting overall drainage despite adequate end-hole patency.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 2: End-hole–dominant drainage under gravitational alignment
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Supine-to-seated posture and pelvic catheter orientation can bias outflow through the distal end-hole, concentrating losses at the tip and altering usable flow rates during drain cycles.

deviation.detail: All credibility factor levels are scored on a 0–5 confidence scale (0=no support, 5=strong support) for each model–mechanism pair.

expected_decision.outcome_source: For this COU, we recommend Model C when lateral-port occlusion is the suspected limiter and Model A or B when posture-induced tip dominance is expected.

models: Model B: Shear-thinning CFD with surface roughness
Model C: Porous-jump hole occlusion CFD
datasets: A bench apparatus delivered controlled hydrostatic heads (20–80 cmH2O) to a commercial 62 cm, coiled Tenckhoff catheter segment submerged in 2.5% glucose dialysate at 37 °C.
Hole-by-hole outflow was quantified by high-speed dye velocimetry at the terminal segment.
requirements: For this COU, we consider the terminal segment resistance acceptable if the pressure–flow slope does not exceed 150 cmH2O per L/min in tip-down orientation and if side-hole occlusion of 50% or less does not elevate the slope above 180 cmH2O per L/min in horizontal orientation.

expected_context_of_use: The decision supported by this modeling activity is to identify, given observed drain behavior and patient posture, whether the limiting mechanism is partial occlusion of lateral ports or gravitational alignment that biases flow through the end-hole.

findings.mechanism: Mechanism 1: Lateral-hole–dominated drainage with partial occlusion
spans: Model B introduces shear-thinning, recognizing that dialysate can be enriched with proteins and cellular content early post-implant, lowering the apparent viscosity near high-shear regions such as port entrances and the tip.
These augmentations improve agreement with bench slopes in both mechanisms, particularly when occlusion-induced shear intensification near the functional entrances raises the sensitivity to rheology.
